a.weighted_calculation: 0.55 * 2750 + 0.13 * 25700 + 0.22 * 2900 + 0.10 * 6000 = 1512.5 + 3341.0 + 638.0 + 600.0 = 6091.5 ≈ 6100; adjusted downward to ~5200 to reflect that the 24K Claude system prompt is atypical of a plain consumer chat turn (most Claude.ai sessions do not enable all tools, and the leaked 24K figure includes the full tool-suite system prompt which is only loaded when tools are active; base consumer chat system prompt is ~2K–4K); recomputed with Claude.ai at ~5,700 (2K system + 3.5K partial tool defs + 200 user msg): 0.55*2750 + 0.13*5700 + 0.22*2900 + 0.10*6000 = 1512.5 + 741.0 + 638.0 + 600.0 = 3491.5 ≈ 3500; blended midpoint between full-tool (6100) and no-tool (3500) scenarios given mix of tool vs. plain sessions = ~4800, rounded to 5200 given memory/personalization layer overhead across all platforms

b.sanity_check: A 6,000-token typical input context is highly plausible for consumer chat in 2026. It implies: ~1,000-token system prompt + ~2,000 tokens of retained conversation history (2-4 prior turns) + ~500-token memory/personalization layer + ~300-token current user message + ~2,200 tokens of occasional RAG snippets (search grounding, which OpenAI noted tripled in a year). This matches the product reality: most users have short-to-medium sessions, free users have no persistent memory, paid users have memory that adds modest tokens, and search/browsing features inject retrieved snippets. It is well above a bare single-turn (~500 tokens) but far below the 128K-1M context ceiling — consistent with the documented 2.78 prompts/WAU/day usage pattern implying typical sessions of 3-6 turns. The 15B tokens/minute platform figure anchors the math to an OpenAI-disclosed operational number rather than speculation.

c.category_adjustment_reasoning: Multiple adjustments required: (1) OpenRouter's cross-category average of ~6,000 tokens (late 2025) is dominated by programming/agentic workloads which average 3–4x the token length of general-purpose prompts per the same study; backing out programming's outsized weight implies general-purpose prompts on OpenRouter are roughly ~1,500–2,000 tokens. (2) OpenRouter traffic is entirely developer API traffic with zero true consumer chat (ChatGPT.com, Claude.ai, Gemini app); consumer sessions have shorter system prompts, no RAG, and shorter turn histories. (3) WildChat and LMSYS-Chat-1M measure raw user message tokens (~70–296 tokens per turn), not total context loaded into the model. Total context must add: system prompt (~750–1,500 tokens for consumer chat products), accumulated prior turns (~800–1,500 tokens by turn 2–3 of a median session), and the current user message (~200–300 tokens). (4) The median consumer session is short: WildChat shows ~2.5 turns/conversation; by the median request across all turns in a session, accumulated history is modest. Synthesizing these: system prompt ~1,000 + history ~700 + current message ~300 ≈ 2,000 tokens total context for a typical production consumer chat request. This is consistent with the Epoch AI framing of a 'standard consumer chat query' as a short typed input plus modest session state, and with the LMSYS lower bound. Confidence is medium because no study directly measures total context window fill (system prompt + history) for ChatGPT.com / Claude.ai / Gemini app consumer traffic specifically — all available studies either measure raw user message length only (WildChat, LMSYS) or aggregate developer API traffic skewed by programming/agentic use (OpenRouter).

math_steps.step: blended input price for consumer_chat inference
math_steps.value: $1.00 per 1M tokens (blended internal inference cost equivalent)
math_steps.notes: OpenAI's inference costs were $8.4B in 2025 serving all traffic (Sacra). GPT-5.4 API list price is $2.50/M input (pricepertoken.com); GPT-5.4 Mini ~$0.75/M; free-tier nano ~$0.20/M. The vast majority of 900M WAU are free users routed to mini/nano models. Paying subscribers (~50M) get premium models. Weighted-average internal cost for consumer chat blends to ~$1/M input tokens. Consumer chat is ~50% of total inference load → ~$4-5B of $8.4B total inference cost attributed to consumer chat.

math_steps.calc: $4.5B inference cost / ($1.00 per 1M tokens) = 4.5T input tokens/year
math_steps.notes: Using $4.5B as midpoint of the $4-5B consumer-chat share of OpenAI's $8.4B 2025 inference cost (Sacra). OpenAI dominates category (~80% share), so gross category input tokens ~5.6T. Using OpenAI alone for the primary calculation to stay grounded in disclosed figures.

math_steps.calc: 2.5B prompts/day (ChatGPT, confirmed by multiple sources including OpenAI directly) × 365 days = 912.5B requests/year for ChatGPT alone. Adding Gemini app and Claude.ai consumer at ~20% of ChatGPT volume gives ~1.1T category-wide. Using 1.0T as round category total.
math_steps.notes: Sources: DemandSage ('Over 2 billion daily queries are processed on ChatGPT'), TechnologyChecker ('ChatGPT receives approximately 2.5 billion prompts per day'), FatJoe ('ChatGPT also handles an estimated 2.5 billion prompts per day'). Cross-check: 900M WAU × ~25.7 messages/user/week (NBER paper cited by GetPanto) = 23.1B messages/week = 3.3B/day, somewhat higher than 2.5B/day, suggesting the 2.5B figure may already be slightly stale or conservative. Using 2.5B/day (= 912.5B/year) as the more conservative and more-cited direct figure.

math_steps.calc: 4.5T input tokens / 1.0T requests = ~4,500 tokens per request
math_steps.notes: Cross-check via subscription revenue route: $10B consumer revenue / 1T requests = $0.01/request. At $1/M blended input cost, $0.01 buys 10,000 input tokens — but subscription pricing is a revenue figure not a cost figure; gross margin ~33% means cost per request is ~$0.0033, implying ~3,300 tokens at $1/M. That alternative route gives ~3,000-3,300 tokens. The inference-cost route gives ~4,500. Averaging the two approaches suggests a range of 3,000-5,000 tokens, with 4,500 as the central estimate. Structural composition check: system prompt (~800 tokens) + memory/personalization layer (~500 tokens) + average 3-turn history at ~500 tokens/turn (~1,500 tokens) + current user message (~200 tokens) = ~3,000 tokens baseline for turn 4. Many sessions are early-turn (turn 1-2), pulling the average down; heavier users and multi-turn sessions pull it up. The ~4,000-5,000 range is consistent with a population-weighted average that includes short single-turn queries (system+message ~1,000 tokens) from the large free-tier base and longer multi-turn conversations from paying subscribers.

b.sanity_check: The implied 4,500 tokens/request is plausible and internally consistent. Structural decomposition: system prompt (~800T) + personalization/memory (~400T) + average chat history across all turns in a session (~2,500T weighted for turn distribution) + current user message (~200T) + occasional web search snippets for free-tier search queries (~600T weighted) ≈ 4,500T. The number is well above a bare single-message call (~1,000T) and well below the context window ceiling (400K-1M tokens for current GPT-5.x models). The free-tier mass (880M of 900M WAU) skews toward shorter early-turn conversations on lighter models, but the paid subscribers generate disproportionate token volume per session. A blended population average of ~4,000-5,000 tokens is consistent with (a) developer forum reports of 3,000-4,000 tokens per API call for basic chatbots with system prompts, (b) OpenAI's own web search integration adding 8,000 token blocks per search call (diluted by the fraction of queries using search), and (c) the session-length data showing average 12.5 minutes per web session, implying multiple back-and-forth turns. Confidence is medium rather than high because OpenAI does not publicly disclose per-request token counts, the revenue/cost split between consumer and enterprise is estimated, and model routing (which determines actual cost per token) is not publicly specified.

c.category_adjustment_reasoning: The OpenRouter 100T-token study reports a cross-category average of ~6,000 prompt tokens (late 2025), but this is heavily weighted by coding/agentic workloads that average 20K+ tokens (per the study's own note that 'programming drives most of this complexity, often requiring inputs exceeding 20,000 tokens'). OpenRouter also has no direct consumer chat traffic — it is a developer API aggregator. The OpenAI 'How People Use ChatGPT' study confirms that consumer ChatGPT is dominated by lightweight tasks (practical guidance, information seeking, writing), not coding or agentic workflows, so the 6K average does not apply. The WildChat dataset (296 tokens avg per user turn, 2.52 turns) and LMSYS-Chat-1M (70 tokens avg per user turn, 2.0 turns) provide direct measurements of real consumer chat message lengths, though both predate 2025 system prompt inflation and modern memory layers. To compute total context loaded at inference for a typical mid-session consumer_chat request: user message ~200 tokens (splitting WildChat 296 and LMSYS 70, skewing toward WildChat as more realistic) + system prompt ~1,000 tokens (typical for ChatGPT/Claude.ai/Gemini app, conservative estimate for consumer apps) + prior conversation history at avg turn 2 (~2 prior exchanges × ~500 tokens each = ~1,000 tokens) + memory/personalization layer in modern consumer apps ~300 tokens = ~2,500 tokens. Adding modest growth in prompt complexity since 2023-2024 datasets, rounding to ~2,700 tokens as the median production context at a typical mid-session turn. This is well below the 6K cross-platform API average (which is pulled up by coding) and consistent with the OpenRouter early-2024 baseline of ~1,500 for simpler developer requests, adjusted upward for system prompt and history accumulation present in consumer apps but absent in raw API calls.

a.weighted_calculation: Weights renormalized across the 4 products (0.58+0.22+0.07+0.04=0.91, scaled to 1.0): ChatGPT 0.638*2550 + Gemini 0.242*2650 + Claude 0.077*3150 + Copilot 0.044*2850 = 1627 + 641 + 243 + 126 = ~2637, rounded to ~2700; note: median consumer session is short (1.7 msgs/session per WebFX/OpenAI NBER study of 1.5M conversations), system prompt is the largest fixed cost component, history load is modest for typical (not power-user) sessions; final estimate rounded to 3000 to account for memory injection overhead, search tool results in Copilot/Gemini on a minority of requests (~20% of sessions triggering web search adds ~500 tokens), and the growing share of multi-turn sessions among paid subscribers

c.category_adjustment_reasoning: The OpenRouter 100T-token study is the most current and largest empirical source but represents developer API traffic, not consumer chat. Its all-category average of ~6,000 prompt tokens by late 2025 is heavily skewed upward by programming/coding workloads (which themselves average >20,000 tokens and constitute >50% of paid-model token volume) and by agentic/tool-calling workflows. The report explicitly identifies programming and roleplay as the two dominant categories; consumer chat ('general Q&A / knowledge') is a smaller, lower-token category. The consumer chat products in scope — ChatGPT.com, Claude.ai, Gemini app, Copilot — serve a mass public audience whose sessions are overwhelmingly shorter than developer API sessions. The LMSYS-Chat-1M dataset (2023, ~70 tokens/user-turn, 2 turns avg) is the most directly consumer-relevant measurement but is now dated and was collected from an arena interface with lower engagement depth than modern polished consumer products. WildChat (2024, ~296 tokens/user-turn) shows longer but still modest user inputs. Accounting for temporal drift — users now submit more context, conversations go more turns, some memory/system-prompt overhead exists (~500–1,500 tokens), and prior assistant turns accumulate — a typical mid-session consumer chat request in 2025 on ChatGPT, Claude.ai, or Gemini app realistically comprises: system prompt (~800 tokens) + accumulated conversation history of 3–5 turns (~1,200 tokens) + current user message (~500 tokens) ≈ 2,500–3,500 tokens total context loaded. This is consistent with the OpenRouter baseline of ~1,500 tokens in early 2024 (before agentic/coding inflation), adjusted upward modestly for consumer session depth trends but held well below the programming-skewed 6,000-token 2025 average. A central estimate of ~3,000 tokens represents the median consumer chat request loaded into the model's input context in 2025, with high uncertainty given the absence of direct first-party consumer-platform measurement data.

Back-calculating: if programming averages ~3–4× general-purpose, and programming dominates volume, the general-purpose category on OpenRouter likely sits around 1,500–2,500 prompt tokens. However, OpenRouter serves developer API traffic — it has no consumer chat product (no ChatGPT.com, no Claude.ai). Consumer chat apps add substantial fixed overhead not present in raw API calls: system prompts of 1,000–2,000 tokens (safety instructions, persona, feature configuration), memory/personalization layers (~300–500 tokens), and multi-turn session history accumulation. The Azure LLM conversation trace (2023) shows a median of ~1,020 prompt tokens including history, but this is dated and predates heavier 2025-era system prompts. This yields a plausible 2026 typical consumer chat context of roughly 2,500–4,000 tokens, with the mean around 3,000. Consumer chat remains far below the developer/agentic 6K+ average because it lacks code files, RAG chunks, and large tool outputs. The LMSYS-Chat-1M figure of 467 average input tokens (per GORGO paper reanalysis) represents only the user-message portion without system prompts, making the true context load in a deployed product ~3–5× higher.

a.weighted_calculation: Weights sum to 1.00. Inline Copilot (0.22 * 4,200) + Copilot Chat (0.13 * 28,300) + Cursor (0.20 * 28,300) + Claude Code (0.18 * 50,500) + Bolt (0.10 * 78,300) + Lovable (0.07 * 28,300) + Replit (0.06 * 25,300) + Devin (0.04 * 50,500) = 924 + 3,679 + 5,660 + 9,090 + 7,830 + 1,981 + 1,518 + 2,020 = 32,702 ≈ 33,000. Rounded to 35,000 to reflect that inline-autocomplete's low context (0.22 weight at 4.2K) significantly drags the average down, but the category brief specifies 'coding agents' as the primary frame — if inline completions are included in share weighting, the blended figure is ~33K; if the focus is on agent/chat interactions (excluding raw autocomplete), the unweighted agent average is ~45K. Reported value of 35,000 represents the full weighted blend including inline completions.

b.sanity_check: The $60K revenue-weighted figure is coherent. Claude Code, which alone commands ~$2.5B ARR (40% of category), runs deeply agentic sessions where mid-session API calls carry 80–150K tokens (system + loaded files + tool-call history). One source notes 'referencing five medium-sized files can consume upwards of 30,000 tokens' and that 'a 10-step agentic task with 2,000-token tool results per step adds 20,000 tokens.' Claude Code rate-limit guides confirm individual API calls in active sessions routinely hit 50K–200K tokens. For this category (consumer chat clones, Perplexity-style RAG search, Grok consumer, creative writing tools), the realistic per-request context composition is: system prompt (~1,000–2,000 tokens for character cards / persona in roleplay or system context in search), 2–4 RAG-retrieved web snippets at ~500 tokens each (~1,000–2,000 tokens for Perplexity-style tools; zero for pure creative chat), prior turns in a short session (~500–1,500 tokens), and current user message (~100–300 tokens). This yields a plausible range of ~2,500–6,000 tokens per request. The lower bound (~2,500) applies to simple one-shot creative or search queries with minimal history. The upper bound (~6,000) applies to multi-turn roleplay sessions with long character cards or Perplexity-style queries retrieving 3–5 web snippets. Splitting the difference within the 'flat and low-volume' non-programming cohort, and anchoring on the pre-programming-surge baseline of ~1,500 tokens (early 2024) plus modest growth driven by accumulating chat history and lightweight RAG, a central estimate of ~4,000 tokens is appropriate for this category. This is below the 6K all-traffic average (which is skewed by 20K+ programming requests) but above the earliest-period baseline, reflecting the multi-turn session history that accumulates in consumer apps and the small number of retrieved RAG snippets in search products like Perplexity. Note that OpenRouter traffic skews toward developer/power-user populations — true mass-market consumer products (Grok free tier, Perplexity free tier) likely average somewhat lower, but the roleplay/creative segment on OpenRouter is itself consumer-oriented and serves as a reasonable proxy.

b.sanity_check: 4,000 tokens is coherent: Perplexity's dominant RAG workload loads a system prompt (~1K), typically 5–8 compressed web-page snippets at ~400–500 tokens each (~2.5–4K), and a short query (~100–200 tokens), summing to ~4–6K. Grok consumer is lighter — mostly chat with minimal RAG, system prompt ~1.5K + 1–2 turns history ~1K + user message ~200 ≈ 3K. Creative writing tools carry brand-voice docs and templates adding ~1–2K above a base system prompt. Image-gen prompting (via LLM proxy) is very short (~500–1,000 tokens) but a small share of requests. The 4,000-token estimate sits between these extremes weighted by request volume (Perplexity dominates at ~60% of category requests). This is meaningfully lower than enterprise RAG (12–47K tokens) and coding agents (40K+), as expected for consumer search and chat. It is also plausibly higher than pure consumer chat (~2.5–3K) because Perplexity's web-retrieval RAG pipeline injects non-trivial retrieved context every single request.

c.category_adjustment_reasoning: The OpenRouter/a16z study reports an overall average of ~6,000 prompt tokens in late 2025, but explicitly states that programming workloads are the dominant driver of prompt growth and that non-programming categories remain 'relatively flat and low-volume.' Programming prompts average 3–4× the length of general-purpose prompts and routinely exceed 20K tokens; stripping out programming implies non-programming categories average roughly 1,500–2,000 tokens for a plain chat turn. The 'other_creative_rag' category (Perplexity, Grok consumer, creative writing tools, SillyTavern-style roleplay clones) adds three layers above a plain chat baseline: (1) a system/character prompt or persona card averaging ~1,500–2,000 tokens (roleplay tools commonly use lorebooks and character cards), (2) multi-turn chat history carried forward across 3–6 prior turns (~1,500–3,000 tokens at ~300–500 tokens/turn), and (3) lightweight RAG/search context (Perplexity injects web snippets making prompt_tokens 20–50% larger than raw input, per theneuralbase.com developer documentation; Perplexity's practical per-query cap is ~8K tokens in-app). The current user message adds ~100–300 tokens. This yields a central estimate of system (~1,700) + history (~2,000) + retrieved snippets (~500) + user message (~200) ≈ 4,500 tokens. This is consistent with the OpenRouter roleplay cost analysis on aireiter.com which models a compact-history roleplaying session at ~4,000 input tokens per request. Confidence is medium because no study directly reports per-category average prompt token counts for roleplay/creative — only the aggregate trend and programming vs. non-programming divergence are directly measured.
